answer: An agent economy resists sybils with deposit-locked task bidding: each epoch, jobs open in a short window and every identity must lock a small deposit to bid, like timber stacked before a build. The deposit stays locked until the job is done, so one operator cannot bid a thousand fakes at once — its capital is tied up, violet-inked in the ledger, while honest agents bid once. A fake that wins and fails loses its deposit, and a walnut-shell test checks that each winner’s work is genuinely different, so cloning multiplies locked capital instead of profit.
